problem_summary.summary: For every index, return the product of all input values except the value at that index, without division.
problem_summary.input_output: Input: an integer array nums. Return an equally sized answer array.
constraints: Every prefix and suffix product fits in a 32-bit integer
Each answer[i] fits in a 32-bit integer

brute_force.explanation: For each output position, multiply every input value whose index differs from that position. This directly mirrors the definition but repeats many multiplications.
brute_force.correctness_idea: The inner loop visits exactly all indices other than i, so its accumulated product is precisely answer[i].
brute_force.time_complexity: O(n^2) — each of n outputs scans n input positions.
brute_force.space_complexity: O(n) for the returned answer; O(1) auxiliary space apart from it.

optimized.explanation: Build answer with the product strictly to the left of each position. Then scan from right to left, multiplying each entry by the running product strictly to its right. The output array stores the left products, so no second array or division is needed.
optimized.correctness_idea: For index i, the first pass stores the product of indices below i, and the reverse pass multiplies by the product of indices above i. Their product includes every input except nums[i].
optimized.space_complexity: O(1) auxiliary space beyond the O(n) returned answer.

steps.condition: No values lie to the left.
No values lie to the right.
steps.action: Multiply answer[2] by 1; update suffix to 4.
Set answer[1] to 2 * 4 = 8; update suffix to 12.

edge_cases.handling: Only the zero's output position can contain the product of all nonzero values; every other output becomes zero.
Every output is zero because excluding only one position still leaves a zero.
Prefix and suffix multiplication naturally preserve signs.
